restore.//: Restore NuGet packages for the API.

build.//: Build the Trax + HotChocolate GraphQL API (net10.0).

db.//: One-shot: bring up the atlas Postgres. Prefers docker, falls back to podman (this machine aliases docker=podman at the shell level, which nx's /bin/sh does not see). Terminates, so it is a valid dependsOn for serve and downstream live-data targets.

commands: if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then docker compose up -d; else podman compose up -d; fi

db:down.//: Stop the Postgres container (keeps the volume). Add --volumes to also drop seeded data.

commands: if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then docker compose down; else podman compose down; fi

db:reset.//: DESTRUCTIVE clean-slate: drop the Postgres volume and bring it back up empty, so the next `serve` rebuilds EVERY atlas table from the current EF model and reseeds. Use this whenever a commit adds/changes a column — `CreateMissingObjectsAsync` is additive by object NAME (creates missing tables/indexes) and never ALTERs an existing table's columns, so a pre-existing volume silently keeps the old schema and either crashes startup (a new index on a missing column, e.g. port_edges.edge_id) or errors a resolver at runtime (e.g. ports.conditionality → portRows `Unexpected Execution Error`). Card re-seed streams ~38k from Scryfall unless dumps/oracle-cards.json exists (fast local path).

commands: if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then docker compose down --volumes; else podman compose down --volumes; fi
if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then docker compose up -d; else podman compose up -d; fi

serve.//: Run the GraphQL server at http://localhost:55250/trax/graphql (self-seeds Scryfall on first run). dependsOn db brings Postgres up first; the server itself is long-running, so it can never be a dependsOn of anything else — depend on 'db' or a future one-shot 'data' target instead.

watch.//: Hot-reload dev server (dotnet watch run) at :55250.
